title: Heidelberg — Neckarwiese, Alte Brücke & Schlossblick
short_pitch: Classic Rhein-Neckar after-work loop: Neckar cycle path, Alte Brücke postcard views, and an e-bike-friendly climb toward Schloss and the Philosophenweg lookouts.

pois.name: Theodor-Heuss-Brücke / Bismarckplatz
pois.why_good: Central Neckar crossing with bike lanes that drops you straight onto the Neuenheim river meadows.

pois.name: Neckarwiese
pois.why_good: Heidelberg’s big riverside lawn between Theodor-Heuss- and Ernst-Walz-Brücke, with a paved Neckar Valley Cycle Path along the bank.

pois.name: Kiosk do Bairro / Café Bairro Neuenheim
pois.why_good: Neighborhood café stop at the Neckarwiese playground kiosk (and parent café on Neuenheimer Marktplatz) for coffee right on the loop.

pois.name: Philosophengärtchen / Merianausblick
pois.why_good: The iconic castle–Altstadt–Neckar panorama opposite the Old Town; reach via the paved Philosophenweg approach from Neuenheim (avoid the stepped Schlangenweg).

pois.name: Alte Brücke (Karl-Theodor-Brücke)
pois.why_good: 1788 sandstone Neckar bridge linking Neuenheim and the Altstadt — Heidelberg’s most photogenic river crossing for bikes.

pois.name: Heidelberger Schloss
pois.why_good: Red-sandstone castle ruin above the Altstadt; the road climb is steep but e-bike friendly and rewards with terrace views over the Neckar valley.

title: Mannheim — Schloss, Rheinpromenade & Waldpark
short_pitch: Flat Quadratestadt nature spin: from the Baroque palace down Stephanienufer along the Rhine, through Waldpark floodplain paths, then back via the Strandbad.

pois.name: Mannheimer Schloss
pois.why_good: One of Europe’s largest Baroque palaces; the Ehrenhof is the official start of Mannheim’s Rhine–Waldpark bike outing.

pois.name: Wasserturm Friedrichsplatz
pois.why_good: Mannheim’s Art Nouveau landmark and city pin — easy to clip onto the loop before dropping toward the Rhine.

pois.name: Rheinpromenade / Stephanienufer
pois.why_good: Tree-lined Rhine bank through Lindenhof with ship traffic views and continuous bike-friendly promenade asphalt.

pois.name: Waldpark Mannheim
pois.why_good: Mannheim’s green lung of floodplain forest and meadow paths where the promenade turns into quiet park riding.

pois.name: Bellenkrappen (Reißinsel edge)
pois.why_good: Calm Old Rhine arm beside the Reißinsel nature reserve — ride the paved park paths along the water (bikes stay outside the core NSG).

pois.name: PURiNO Strandbad am Rhein
pois.why_good: Italian riverside restaurant on stilts at Strandbadweg 1 — the classic post-ride pasta/pizza stop before spinning back to the city.

title: Heidelberg foothills — Boxberg, Bierhelderhof & Gaisberg gravel
short_pitch: Corridor-friendly Königstuhl foothills loop: compacted forest roads from Rohrbach–Boxberg up to Bierhelderhof and the Gaisberg viewpoints without committing to the full 700 hm summit circuit.

pois.name: Heidelberg-Kirchheim/Rohrbach Bahnhof
pois.why_good: Rhine-Neckar S-Bahn stop on the Wiesloch–Heidelberg line — ideal Discover staging for riders arriving from the corridor.

pois.name: Boxberg forest roads
pois.why_good: Entry into the Königstuhl massif’s gravel Forstwege above Rohrbach, used by local gravel and MTB loops toward Kohlhof and Gaisberg.

pois.name: Bierhelderhof
pois.why_good: Historic farm-inn on a clearing at ~260 m with beer garden, Hofladen, and a natural mid-loop pause above Rohrbach.

pois.name: Ehrenfriedhof Heidelberg
pois.why_good: Hillside memorial cemetery on the Speyerer Hof / Gaisberg approach, a quiet landmark on the forest-road network.

pois.name: Gaisbergturm & Mammutbäume
pois.why_good: Lookout tower on the 376 m Gaisberg with Rhine-plain views, next to the 1870s sequoia arboretum — the scenic high point of a ~60–75 min foothills spin.
